name: CIFAR-10 decision-based adversarial attack
description: Write a Python draw_proposals(org_img, best_adv_img, std_normal_noise, hyperparams) function that proposes the next point of an L2 decision-based random-walk attack on a CIFAR-10 ResNet-18; scored by the mean L2 distance between 20 correctly classified test images and their adversarial examples after 2,500 queries per image (lower is better).

sources.locator: core/attacks/EVOAttack_template.py (EvoAttack loop, f(p), 120 s abort), core/search_utils/task.py (draw_proposals contract)

requirements.hardware: See upstream requirements and task notes.
requirements.datasets: 100 randomly selected CIFAR-10 images per class and ResNet18 target

evaluation.paper_metric: mean/median L2 adversarial perturbation versus query count

commands.notes: Standalone decision-based attack evaluation with the shipped heuristic (no model calls; downloads a RobustBench CIFAR-10 model, PyTorch).
EvoEngineer search for attack heuristics. Model-driven search: requires LLM API credentials and incurs cost; never run by seed checks.

setup_instructions: pip install uv; uv sync (resolves PyTorch cu128)
Original standalone implementation is on the v1 branch
framework_setup_instructions: pip install uv; uv sync (resolves PyTorch cu128)
Original standalone implementation is on the v1 branch

limitations: The paper and project sources examined link no runnable official repository; the release was identified separately and is pinned (see below).
Upstream commands and dependencies were inspected; costly training, paid APIs, and hardware experiments were not executed.

The matching pgg3/L-AutoDA repository has no README/license in the inspected tree; run_attack.py defaults to BoundaryAttack and evaluates only one batch, so it is not a paper evaluation command without changes.
Execution interface inspected in pinned source. Full paper experiments have not been reproduced here.
